Ylang Ylang Extra

Cananga odorata

The first and finest fraction of the distillation.

Heady, creamy and intensely floral — closer to banana and jasmine than to rose. 'Extra' is the first fraction drawn off the still, where the delicate top notes still survive; later fractions are cheaper and noticeably flatter.

How to use

  • Diffuse 2 drops — this one is far stronger than it smells on the bottle.
  • Dilute to 1% for a warm, floral body oil.
  • Blend a single drop into sweet orange to round off the citrus.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Scent profile

  • Creamy floral
  • Ripe banana
  • Faint spice

What's in it

  • 100% pure Cananga odorata flower oil

Who it's for

People who like heavy florals

Among the most intensely floral oils there is. If jasmine and tuberose appeal, this will.

Blenders rounding off citrus

A single drop takes the sharp edge off an orange or bergamot blend without reading as floral.

Anyone curious about perfumery

A textbook example of how fractional distillation changes an oil, and a good one to learn on.

What people get wrong

Using it at the same rate as everything else. Two drops is a diffuser's worth. At five it stops smelling like flowers and starts smelling like a headache, and that reputation is almost entirely a dosing problem.

Buying on price without checking the grade. Extra, I, II and III are fractions drawn off the same still at different points. III is far cheaper and noticeably flatter, and the grade is often left off the label.

What it won't do

It is genuinely polarising. A meaningful number of people find ylang ylang cloying at any dose, and there is no dilution that fixes that — it is a preference, not a technique.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Ylang Ylang Extra

What does 'Extra' mean?

It is the first fraction drawn off the still, taken in the first hour or so of distillation, when the lightest and most delicate compounds come across. Later fractions — I, II and III — are cheaper and progressively flatter.

Why do some people dislike it?

It is very rich and very sweet, and at anything above a couple of drops it becomes overwhelming for many people. Try it at one drop in a blend before committing to diffusing it alone.

Does it blend well with anything?

Citrus, particularly bergamot and sweet orange, where it adds body without taking over. Also sandalwood, if you want something warm and heavy.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Around 2% for the body — roughly 12 drops per 30 ml of carrier oil — and 1% for the face. Always patch-test before wider use, and never apply neat.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Mumbai within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
